newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA'S INKATHA DISCUSSES CONSTITUTION WITH NP.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA'S INKATHA DISCUSSES CONSTITUTION WITH NP.

text.p: South Africa's two main opposition parties, the Inkatha Freedom Party and the National Party (NP), met on Saturday for "constructive" talks on whether Inkatha would end its boycott of the constitutional assembly, the NP said.

"The meeting was very constructive," a statement said. "The IFP explained its preferences regarding changes to the constitutional text and the NP delegation described its viewpoints regarding those issues referred back by the constitutional court."
Earlier this month the court ruled that some aspects of the new constitution did not comply with principles laid down in multi-party talks and had to be redrafted.

This raised the possibility that Inkatha, which boycotted the constitution-making process in protest at the African National Congress having reneged on an agreement for international mediation, might return to the constitutional assembly to contribute to drafting amendments.
"The NP delegation strongly encouraged the IFP to rejoin the proceedings of the constitutional assembly as soon as possible," the statement said.
"The IFP will now prepare specific proposals especially regarding the constitutional position and role of traditional authorities, whereafter the parties will meet again."
The statement said those at the meeting included Roelf Meyer and Sam de Beer from the NP and Walter Felgate and Ben Ngubane from Inkatha.
Inkatha held a similar meeting with the ANC earlier this week.
